A. F. Hasan Arif; Senior Advocate, instructed by Mrs. Mahmuda Begum, Advocate-on-Record ----- For the Appellants

Vs.

case_source: (From the Judgment and decree dated 17.05.2001 passed by the High Court Division in First Appeal No. 116 of 1996)
full_judgment:
Hasan Foez Siddique J.:- This appeal at the instance of the plaintiffs by leave to consider the legality of the judgment and decree dated 17.05.2001 passed by the third Judge of the High Court Division allowing' the First Appeal No.116 of 1996 and dismissing the suit upon setting aside the judgment and decree dated 23.11.1995 passed by the Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka, in Title Suit No. 255 of 1993. Earlier a Division Bench of the High Court Division delivered dissenting judgment on 01.08.2000 in the said appeal.

<u>2. The relevant facts for the disposal of the appeal, in short, are that the appellants instituted the aforesaid suit for declaration of their title in the suit covering an area of 1.20 acres of C.S. Plot No. 1 appertaining to C.S. Khatian No. 53 of Mouza Kakrail., Police Station Ramna, (former Keranigonj) Dhaka alleging, inter alia, that the suit land along with other lands measuring 48.90 acres of said Plot and Khatian corresponding to S.A. Plot No.64 and S.A. Khatian No. 26 originally belonged to Bhawal Zaminder Rajkumer Rabindra Narayan Roy Chowdhury who settled the suit land to Ashraf Ali Kazi, the predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiffs executing a pattannama on 05.02.1905. Said Ashraf Ali Kazi took over possession of the suit land and paid rent to the Zaminder. In C.S. operation, the suit land along with other lands of the disputed jam, was recorded in the name of Public Works Department under Bharat Samrat. Against the said record of right Ashraf Ali Kazi filed objection to get the same corrected and got an order on 24.05.1925. In S.A. operation the same was again recorded in the name of Public Works Department. On 12.01.1992, the plaintiffs discovered the pattannama, rent receipts and mutated C.S. Khatian in an old box in their house. On 08.03.1992, they collected the certified copies of the S.A. and C.S. Khatians and confirmed about the erroneous preparation of S.A. record of right. Thereafter, they filed this suit.</u>

3. The defendant-respondents contested the suit by filing a written statement denying all the that the suit land along with other lands covering 48.90 acres originally belonged to Public Works Department under Bharat Samrat. Accordingly, the same was recorded in C.S. Plot No. 1 and khatian No. 53. Subsequently the Deputy. Commissioner, Dhaka took over possession of the suit land. The story of settlement of the plaintiffs from Bhawal Rajkumar Rabindra Narayan Roy Chowdhury is false and the document produced by the plaintiffs are forged and fabricated. The C.S. Khatian had not been corrected at the instance of the plaintiffs' predecessor. The corrected Khatian produced by the plaintiffs is forged. The Government has been possessing the suit land. The Government started to construct buildings in the suit land for residential purpose of higher Government Officials. The S.A. record of right was duly prepared in the name of the Government. The suit should be dismissed.

4. The trial Court by his judgment and decree dated 11.09.1995 decreed the suit. The defendant- respondents preferred First Appeal No. 116 of 1996 in the High Court Division. A Division Bench of the High Court Division comprised by Mr. Justice Md. Mozammel Haque and Mr. Justice Md. Abdur Rashid heard the said appeal. Mr. Justice Md. Mozammel Haque by his judgment dismissed the appeal. On the other hand, Mr. Justice Md. Abdur Rashid allowed the appeal and set aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court. Then the said appeal was heard by Mr. Justice Md. Tafazzal Islam as third Judge who by the impugned judgment and decree dated 16th and 17th May, 2001 allowed the appeal on setting aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court. Against the judgment and decree passed by Mr. Justice Md. Tafazzal Islam, the plaintiff-appellants preferred this appeal getting leave.

5. Leave was granted to consider the sub-missions of the appellants that the plaintiffs having proved their permanent settlement of the year 1905 producing pattanama (Ext.1) and the rent receipts of the years 1907, 1912, 1928, 1932, 1938, 1940, 1945 and 1948 (Exhibit-2 series proved their title in the suit land as well as their uninterrupted possession in the same over 87 years, the third Judge of the High Court Division erred in law in dismissing the suit. The Second submission was that the pattannama (exhibit-1) written in the year 1905 on stamp paper of more than 30 years old and the value of the land was shown at 11.15/- only and in such view of the matter, the same was not required to be registered under Section 17 of the Registration Act. The next point was that the plaintiffs' predecessor Ashraf Ali Kazi paid rents to the landlord vide exhibit-2 series are the best piece of evidence of possession of the plaintiffs in .the suit land. It was further pointed out that the C.S. record of right stand corrected on the basis of the objection filed by Ashraf Ali Kazi (exhibit-3 series). It was further pointed out that the documents produced by the plaintiffs were old documents of more than 30 years so as per provision of section 90 of the Evidence Act those documents should be accepted as legal evidence.

6. Mr. A.F. Hasan Arif, the senior Counsel 'appearing on behalf of the appellants, submits that the predecessors-in-interest of the plaintiff-appellants got the suit land by way of settlement in the year 1905 and produced more than 30 years old pattannama (exhibit-1) . The plaintiffs paid rents to the Zaminder vide Exhibit-2 series and they got the C.S. Khatian corrected vide exhibit-3 series and had been possessing the suit land more than 87 years. The third Judge of the High Court Division has committed an error of law in disbelieving the pattannama, corrected C.S. Khatian and rent receipts. He submits that the findings of the third Judge of the High Court Division regarding authenticity of exhibit-1 made in an old British Indian Stamp of 1905, and the rent receipts (exhib-it-2 series), the corrected C.S. Khatian (exhibit 3 series) and exhibit-4, the volume book of Government containing C.S. Khatian are erroneous. He further submits that since price of the land was Tk. 15/- only as it appears in the pattannama, the same was not required to he registered under section 17 of the Registration Act.

7. Mr. Goutom Kumar, the learned Deputy Attorney General appearing on behalf of the respondents, submits that the High Court Division on vivid discussions on the materials on record came to the conclusion that the pattannama, rent receipts of the Zamindar and corrected C.S. Khatian are forged and fabricated documents. He submits that Mr. Justice Md. Abdur Rashid rightly directed to prosecute the plaintiff-appellants initiating proceeding under Section 476 read with 195 (1) (c) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, on allegation of forging those documents. He submits that the plaintiffs had no title-and possession in the suit land. The Government, constructing the buildings in the suit land; has been possessing the same. The instant suit was not at all maintainable without the prayer for recovery of khas possession.

8. We have heard the learned Advocate for the appellants and the learned Deputy Attorney General for the respondent perused the judgment of the courts below and other materials on record.

9. The case of the plaintiffs is that their predecessor Ashraf Ali Kazi took settlement of the suit land on the basis of pattannama dated 05.02.1995 (exhibit-i). P.W.1 Abdul Matin Kazi, who was about 67 years old at the time of adducing his evidence on 19.08.1994 (that is, he was born after 22 years of alleged execution of the said pattannama) in his evidence, inter alia, said, এই সেই পত্তন নামার মূল কপি প্রঃ- ১ হিসাবে চিহ্নিত। কোর্ট দাখিল করিলাম। বিবাদীপক্ষে এই মর্মে আপত্তি যে, লেখা অষ্পষ্ট ও ছেড়া প্রঃ ১টি। নোটারি পাবলিক কর্তৃক প্রত্তন নামার সত্যায়িত টাইপ কপি দাখিল করিলাম। প্রঃ ১(ক) আপত্তি সহকারে”। The is, exhibit-1 and 1(Ka) had been admitted in evidence with objection. The plaintiffs examined P.W.2 Sailendra Nath Sarker, a man of 78 years old, to prove the pattannama. In his cross-examination he said " ১নং প্রদর্শনী পড়তে পারব না।" From his evidence it appears that this witness was horn sometime in 1916, that is, after 11 years of the alleged execution of the pattannama. In order to substantiate the contents of the pattannama, the plaintiffs produced a notarized copy of the said pattannama exhibit-1(ka) P.W. 2 admitted that contents of the exhibit-1 are not readable. The plaintiffs did not examine the writer of the duplicated pattannama nor they examined the notary public, who notarized the same. In such view of the matter, Ext.1(Ka) could not be relied on. In the case of Harihar Prashad Vs. Desnarain reported in AIR 1956 SC 305 it was observed that the presumption enacted in Section 90 of the Evidence Act can be raised only with reference to original documents not to copies thereof. Furthermore, it appears that from Ext.1(Ka) that Ext.1 had been executed by Sree Kamini Kumar Bandapadhya on behalf of Kumar Rabindra Narayan Roy Chowdhury. The P.W. 2, who claimed to be the Tahsilder of Bhawal Estate and joined in the said Estate in 1346 B.S., did not say in his evidence that Sree Kamini Kumar Bandapadhya was the Manager of Kumar Rabindra Narayan Roy Chowdhury, the Zaminder of Bhawal Estate. The plaintiffs failed to produce any other evidence to prove that Kamini Kumar Bandapadhya was the manager of the Estate.

<u>10. Submission of Mr. Arif is that since the Ext. 1 Pattannama is an old document of more than 30 years and had been produced from proper custody, the court would presume that the signature and every other part of Ext.1 is that person's hand writing and, the same had been duly executed by the person by whom it purports to be executed as per provision of Section 90 of the Evidence Act. The spirit of section 90 of the Evidence Act is that if private documents not less than thirty years old are produced from proper custody and are on their face free from suspicion, the court may presume at they w have been signed or written by the persons whose signatures they bear or in whose hand writing they purport to he, that they have been duly attested and executed, if they purport so to he Section 90 only lays down that the court may presume that document purporting to be 30 years old are genuine. That it must not presume them to be so. Supreme Court of India in the case of Sri Lakhi Baruah Vs. Sri Padma Kanta Kalita reported in AIR 1996 SC 1253 observed that Section 90 of the Evidence Act is founded on necessity and convenience because it is extremely difficult and sometimes not possible to lead evidence to prove handwriting, signature or execution of old documents after lapse of 30 years. In order to obviate such difficulties or improbabilities to prove execution of an old documents section 30 has been incorporated in the Evidence Act, which does away with the strict rule of proof of private documents. Presumption of genuineness may he raised if the document in question is produced from proper custody. It is, however, the discretion of the Court to accept the presumption flowing from Section. The presumption is permissive and accordance no the circumstances of each case the court may or may not raise it. That is, such presumption discretionary and so where a document is suspicious on the face of it or mutilated, the court may refuse to make presumption. It is not obligatory on a court to raise the presumption. The language being "may" when the person who has been examined as P.W.2 to prove the Ext.1 himself has said “১নং প্রদর্শনী পড়তে পারবো না"; then why the court will rely upon such document .At the time of making exhibit the defendant raised objection saving, লেখা অষ্পষ্ট ও ছেড়া প্রঃ ১টি। In such circumstances, the provision of section 90 ought to be applied with more care and great caution because nothing can he more easy than, for an unscrupulous ours person, who is wrongfully in possession and wants to make out a title to it to forge such document in his favour more than 30 years old and produce it as the proper custodian relieving himself of the necessity of proving its execution. The Ext. 1 patina must not be presumed to he genuine merely from its being ancient. Some other evidence were required to be given of the early existence and publicity of Ext. 1 . Neither C. S. khatian nor S. A. khatian had been prepared on the basis of Ext. 1.</u>

11. In order to show the existence and publicity of Ext.1 or in other words to prove the story of their settlement dated 11.02.1905 and rebut the presumption under Section 103. B of the Bengal Tenancy Act, which is available in favour of the Government since C.S. record of right was prepared in favour of the Government ( Ext. A), the plaintiffs produced Ext .2 series, the Zamindari dakhilas and alleged corrected khatian Ext. 3 series. It is the claim of the plaintiffs that against C.S. Khatian their predecessor Ashraf Ali Kazi filed Objection Case No. 327H/1932 and got his name corrected in the Zamindery Sherista and obtained certified copies of the corrected Khatian from Zamindery sherist- Correction of the entry in Khatian filing objection in the Zamindery Sherista is totally illegal. As per provision of Section 108A of the Bengal Tenancy Act, which was transferred as section 115B, by the Bengal Tenancy (Amendment) Act, 1928, only the Revenue Officer specially empowered by the Government on application or of his own motion, within two years (earlier time limit was for 12 months) from the date of certificate of the final publication of the record of right under sub-section (2) of Section 103A, correct any entry in such record of rights which he was satisfied had been made owing to a bonafide mistake. That is, Revenue Officer was legally authorized to correct the Khatian nobody else. The concerned volume regarding P.S. Khatian was called for to ascertain the authenticity of Ext. 3 series which was marked as Ext. 4 . T. Islam, J examined Ext. 3 series, the corrected Khatian produced by the plaintiffs and relevant volume book of C.S. khatian Ext. 4 thoroughly. Such examination, as it appears from his observation that the same was made most carefully which is praise-worthy.

<u>12. The observation in that regard are as follows:</u>

<u>"I have gone through Ext. 4, which is the volume of Mouza 282 Kakrail produced before the trial court. In C.S. Khatian Nos. 1, 2, 9-10, 13, 24, 53 and 55 as contained in Ext. 4, on the top of the front page at the left hand side under the heading  উপরিস্ত স্বত্ব/পরিচয়ে the words "ভারত সম্রাট" have been printed and out of the above Khatian at the right hand side of the Khatian Nos. 1, 2, 9-10, 13-24 under the heading উপরিস্ত স্বত্ব/পরিচয়ে বিস্তারিত দখল the names of different persons were printed and in the remaining C.S. Khatian Nos. 53 and 57, under this very heading at right hands side, public works Department and District Board respectively, both on behalf of Bharat Samrat were printed. In C.S. Khatian Nos. 3, 4, 5, 6 and 17 as contained in Ext. 4 similarly under the heading উপরিস্ত স্বত্ব/পরিচয়ে the word পত্তন রাজেন্দ্র নারায়ণ রায় ৩নং কুমার রবিন্দ্র নারায়ন রায় চৌধুরী ওয়ারিশগণ পক্ষে কোর্ট অফ ওয়ার্ড were printed and out of the above khatian under the heading অত্র স্বত্ব/অত্র স্বত্বের বিস্তারিত দখল of C.S. Khatian Nos.  4,5 and 6 the names of different persons were printed and in C.S. Khatian Nos. 3 and 7 only, and this heading " কুমার রবিন্দ্র নারায়ন রায় চৌধুরী ওয়ারিশগণ পক্ষে কোর্ট অফ ওয়ার্ডস’"Were printed.</u>

<u>In C.S. Khatian Nos. 31-32, 33Ka, 34-35, 39-40, 43, 46-47 and 47Ka as contained in Ext. 4 under the heading উপরিস্তস্বত্ব/পরিচয়ে the words পত্তনী কালীন নারায়ন রায় ৩০নং দখল কুমার রবিন্দ্র নারায়ন রায় চৌধুরী ওয়ারিশগণ পক্ষে কোর্ট অফ ওয়ার্ডস were printed and under the heading অত্র স্বত্ব/অত্র স্বত্বের বিস্তারিত দখল the name of different persons were printed and in C.S. Khatian No. 8, as contained in Ext. 4 under the heading উপরিস্থ স্বত্ব/পরিচয়ে the words মিরস জামাল, ৭নং রবিন্দ্র নারায়ন রায় চৌধুরী ওয়ারিশগণ পক্ষে কোর্ট অফ ওয়ার্ড were printed and under the heading অত্র স্বত্বের বিস্তারিত দখল the name of Sheikh Abdul was printed.</u>

<u>In C.S. Khatian Nos. 30, 51Ka and 51 Kha as contained in Ext. 4, under the heading অত্র স্বত্বের বিস্তারিত দখল the words সিকিম তালুক রামকৃষ্ণ দত্ত were printed and out of the above Khatians, in C.S. Khatian No. 30 under the heading অত্র স্বত্ব/অত্র স্বত্বের বিস্তারিত দখল the words কুমার রবিন্দ্র নারায়ন রায় চৌধুরী ওয়ারিশগণ পক্ষে কোর্ট অফ ওয়ার্ডস were printed and in Khatian No. 51 Ka and 51 Kha under the above heading of অত্র স্বত্বের বিস্তারিত দখল the names of other persons were printed.</u>

<u>In C.S. Khatian No. 25-27 and 51 as contained in Ext. 4 under the heading উপরিসত স্বত্ব/পরিচয়ে the words and also the names of 13 co-sharers of the Zamindari were printed and under the heading অত্র স্বত্ব/অত্র স্বত্বের বিস্তারিত দখল the name of different persons were printed.</u>

<u>Thus in the Khatians mentioned above on the front page on the top at left hand side under the heading উপরিস্ত স্বত্ব/ পরিচয়ে the names of Zamindars were printed and at the right hand side under the heading অত্র স্বত্বের বিস্তারিত দখল the name of tenants/riots were printed and at the over leafs of some of the above Khatians, the names of the possessors were printed.</u>

<u>Regarding C.S. Khatian No. 53 as contains in Ext. 4, as it appears at left hand side under the heading উপরিস্ত স্বত্ব/পরিচয়ে the words উপরিস্ত স্বত্ব/পরিচয়ে the words ভারত সম্রাট were printed and under the heading অত্র স্বত্ব/ অত্র স্বত্বের বিস্তারিত দখল the name of Public Works Department on behalf of Bharat Samrat, have been printed and it is only at the over leaf, Kumar Rabindra Narayan himself was shown as mere possessors of 48.90 acres of land in C.S. Plot No. 1 as stated earlier, in C.S. Khatian Nos. 3-7, 8, 30, 31, 32, 32 Ka 33, 34, 39; 40, 43,47, 51Ka and 51 Kha of Ext. 4 in most of the cases the Court of words of the heirs of Kumar Rabindra Narayan have been shown as Zamindars and in few cases the above court of words have been shown ryot under the heading" অত্র স্বত্বের বিস্তারিত দখল and is none of the above Khatians Kumar Rabindra Narayan himself was not shown as Zamindar or tenant. It thus appears that on 23.04.1917, when the above C.S. Khatian were finally published, Kumar Rabindra Narayan ceased hold any interest in any of the above Khatians and instead the court of wards of his heirs were shown as Zamindar and tenants.</u>

<u>Accordingly how in C.S. Khatian No. 53 as contained in Ext. 4 Kumar Rabindra Narayan could be shown as possessor and like wise how in Ext. 3 also Kumar Rabindra Narayan himself could be shown as Zamindar."</u>

13. It was further observed that the claim of the plaintiffs that Kumar Rabindra Narayan got Zamindari of C.S. plot No. 1 containing 48.90 acres of land has also no basis at all.

<u>14. Mr. Arif failed to satisfy this court making any submission to discard aforesaid findings referring any material on record. The aforesaid findings arrived at by the last court of facts are based evidence. Since Kumer Rabindra Narayon was neither landlord nor tenant in the land recorded in Khatian No. 53 and plot No. 1 no one, claiming himself as manager of Kumer Rabindra Narayon Chowdhury, had any authority to settle the same on his behalf. He was not a person immediately under whom the tenant holds and no tenancy had been established pursuant to Ext. 1 in re sport of the suit land.</u>

15. The C.S. record of right was prepared in the name Public Works Department under Bharat Samrat. Such record of right is evidence of the matter referred to in the entry and should be presumed to be correct until it is proved by evidence to be incorrect. Since such presumption being a statutory one could not be taken away mere by allegation that the same is incorrect. The burden of proving that such entry in the record of right is incorrect is on the party who alleges it. In this case the plaintiffs failed to rebut the presumption by adducing evidence. The documentary evidence produced by the plaintiffs are found to be forged and fraudulent one by the Court of facts.

16. The plaintiffs stated that their predecessor Ashraf Ali Kazi died sometime in 1948. It has also been stated in the plaint that in 1992 the plaintiffs allegedly got the papers produced in the Court in an old box. The plaintiffs did not produce any materials in support of their claim to deal with the property, at least, from 1948 to 1992. They did not take any step to record their names in the khatian and to pay rent to the Government. It is totally unacceptable proposition' that one, who is allegedly in possession in the land and structure thereon within Dhaka City Corporation, would not take any step to record/ mutate his name in the khatian, pay rent, municipal taxes, WASA, Gas bills etc.

17. A controversy has arisen as to whether the instant permanent tenancy can be created otherwise by a registered instrument. The last court of facts held that the suit land is non- agriculture land to be used for non-agricultural purpose. The Contents of pattanipatta or amalnama as reproduced in duplicatted copy (Ext 1Ka) were as follows:

<u>“শ্রী আশ্রাব আলী কাজী, পিতা সোমাকাজী, জাতী মুসলমান, পেশা গৃহস্থী, সাং-হাতীর রাস্তা, থানা কেরানীগঞ্জ, জেলা-ঢাকা। -----পাট্রা গ্রহিতা।</u>

<u>18. From the contents of Ext. 1(Ka), intention of the parties as gathered from those contents; surrounding circumstances and the claim of the plaintiffs it appears to us that the plaintiffs tried to establish that the Ext. 1 is a lease deed which is unregistered and unilateral one in respect of the property described therein and which is to be used for orchard and homestead and the same is a lease in perpetuity. In the case of Safar Ali Master Vs. Abdul Mazid reported in 47 CLJ Page 27 it was observed that homestead land within a municipality even, though recorded as "bagan" land in the record of rights is not governed by the Bengol Tenancy Act but by the Transfer of Property Act. In the case of Ramdas Vs. Bipradas reported in 19 C.W.N. page 35 it was held that tenancies for residential purposes are outside the scope of the Bengol Tenancy Act. We are of the view that the alleged iv lease was to be regulated under the provision of Transfer of Property Act not by the Bengol Tenancy Act. Lease as defined in section 105 of the transfer of Property Act is a transfer of right to enjoy immovable property made for a certain time express or implied, or in perpetuity. In the case of Abdus Satter Vs. Suresh Chandra Das reported in 32 DLR (AD) page 170 it has been observed that the essential elements constituting lease are the following: a) the right must be one as to immovable property, (b) the right must be that enjoyment of immovable property; (c) these must be a transfer of much right; (d) the right of transfer must be made for a certain time, express or implied, or in perpetuity; (f) the consideration must be of the particular kind namely, premium or rent as defined by the section either or both of them. In the case of M.H. Khondker, Advocate Vs. Bangladesh reported in 30 DLR (SC)1 it has been held that (i) by a lease a subordinate interest is created by a person in favour of another person in respect of some immovable property on condition of premium or rent (ii) the right which is created a lease is the right of tenancy 'Lease" and tenancy are cognate terms, implying the same kind of jural relationship. In the case of Bastacolla Colliery Co. Ltd. Vs. Bandhu Beldar reported AIR 1960 Pat 344 it has been observed by the Full Bench of Patna High Court that before amendment of section 107 of the Transfer of Property Act by Act 20 of 1929 a valid lease could be created by a patta executed by the lessor but all leases coming within the first paragraph of Section 107 of the Transfer of Property Act can only be made by registered instrument. Since the instant transaction is a transfer of interest of non- agricultural land and to be used for nonagricultural purpose entitling the leasee the enjoyment of such immovable property which includes the right to possession thereof in perpetuity such tenancy can only be created by registered instrument. An unregistered documents of lease which was required to be registered conveyed no title and created no right of the plaintiffs. Ext. 1 is inoperative under Section 107 of the Transfer of Property Act and could not create a tenancy; could not create the inception of tenancy and could not be considered to find out tenancy. A document which was compulsorily registrable but was not registered is void as regards immovable property which is non agriculture in nature and to be used for non-agricultural purposes.</u>

19. So far possession is concerned the defendants claimed that the Government constructed or started to construct building in the property in question. The evidence as to possession of the plaintiffs are insufficient. In the plaint the plaintiffs, inter alia, stated, বাদীগণ ও নালিশী সম্পত্তি সংক্রান্ত দলিল দস্তাবেস ছাড়া নালিশী সম্পত্তিতে বড় ধরনের নির্মাণ করার জন্য মনের জোর পায় নাই। বাদীগনের পিতা কর্তৃক নালিশী সম্পত্তির চারিদিকে সীমানা নির্ধারণ দেওয়াল ছাড়া অন্য কোন নির্মাণ করে নাই।” In evidence the plaintiff No.1 as P.W.1 deviating the plaint case said “আমার আব্বা অংশ বিশেষ বসবাস করতেন গৃহনির্মান করিয়া বক্রি বংশের সবজীর চাষাবাদ ক্রমে ভোগ দখল করতেন, তাহার জীবনকাল পর্যন্ত।" The plaintiffs failed to produce any paper regarding utility services i.e. DESA, WASA, GAS etc. in support of their claim of possession. On 14th May, 2013 the plaintiff appellants submitted a supplementary paper books producing some papers including information slip in support of their case. The contents of information supplied, inter alia, were: "সরজমিনে তদন্তে দেখা যায় প্রার্থীর জমি গণপূর্ত বিভাগের বাউন্ডারী দেওয়াল দ্বারা বেষ্টিত।” That is, from their papers it appears that the plaintiffs have no possession in the suit land. On due consideration of the evidence on record, the last court of facts rightly found the possession of the defendants in the suit land. The said finding is based on evidence.

<u>20. Since the plaintiff appellants are out of possession, the suit for simple declaration without the prayer for recovery of khas possession was not maintainable.</u>

21. Considering the aforesaid facts and circumstances, we are constrained to hold that it was an ill attempt of the plaintiffs to grab the government property by creating some documents. In such view of the matter Md. Abdur Rashid, J. rightly directed the trial Court to take steps against the plaintiffs drawing proceeding under section 476 read with Section 195(1) (c) of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

22. In view of the facts and circumstances recorded above, we do not find any sub-stance in the appeal.

23. In the result the appeal is dismissed.

End.
